item.title: ECUA Executive Director Jason Yarborough Resigns; Bruce Woody Named Acting Director
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority board accepted Executive Director Jason Yarborough's resignation during a special meeting Friday, according to a statement from ECUA's Public Information Office. Bruce Woody, former ECUA executive director, will step into the role of acting executive director while the authority conducts a search for a…
item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority board accepted Executive Director Jason Yarborough's resignation during a special meeting Friday, according to a statement from ECUA's Public Information Office.

Bruce Woody, former ECUA executive director, will step into the role of acting executive director while the authority conducts a search for a permanent replacement, ECUA said.

No details were provided about the circumstances of Yarborough's departure or a timeline for the executive director search.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Naples Building Official to State Construction Board
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Stephen Beckman to the Construction Industry Licensing Board. Beckman currently serves as director of Building Services for the City of Naples and holds multiple certifications including General Contractor, Building Code Administrator, and Plans Examiner through the Florida Department of…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Stephen Beckman to the Construction Industry Licensing Board. Beckman currently serves as director of Building Services for the City of Naples and holds multiple certifications including General Contractor, Building Code Administrator, and Plans Examiner through the Florida Department of Business Regulation.

Beckman is active in professional organizations, including the Building Officials Association of Florida and the Association of State Floodplain Managers. He earned his bachelor's degree from Concordia College.

The appointment is subject to confirmation by the Florida Senate, according to the Governor's Press Office.

item.title: Milton prioritizes school bus stops for debris removal ahead of reopening
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton is focusing storm debris removal efforts around school bus stops and campuses as Santa Rosa County schools prepare to reopen next week following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued Friday. Crew began collection operations Tuesday, October 13, and are working daily through November to clear an estimated…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is focusing storm debris removal efforts around school bus stops and campuses as Santa Rosa County schools prepare to reopen next week following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued Friday.

Crew began collection operations Tuesday, October 13, and are working daily through November to clear an estimated 400,000 cubic yards of storm debris plus another 35,000 cubic yards of construction and demolition material. Residents may notice debris trucks in neighborhoods collecting some piles while leaving others — the city says crews are prioritizing school-related access first and will return for additional collection as operations progress.

Parents and guardians should keep children closely supervised near bus stops and debris work zones. The city warns of active heavy equipment, utility crews, and recovery activities in neighborhoods. The debris processing site is located about three blocks from Rhodes Elementary School at Byrom and James Streets, where motorists and pedestrians should exercise caution.

Preliminary damage assessments show about 60% of Milton structures sustained some storm damage, with roughly 5% deemed uninhabitable. The city asked residents to remain patient as recovery continues.

item.title: Pensacola State College resuming normal operations Monday after weather closure
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola State College will return to normal operations on Monday, October 19, following a weather-related closure that affected the campus this week. All classes, events, and activities will resume, according to a media alert from the college. College officials say all facilities have been inspected and deemed safe for occupancy, with one…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College will return to normal operations on Monday, October 19, following a weather-related closure that affected the campus this week. All classes, events, and activities will resume, according to a media alert from the college.

College officials say all facilities have been inspected and deemed safe for occupancy, with one exception: the Milton Campus Library will remain closed pending repairs. Employees at that location will report to the Pensacola Campus Library instead, while all other staff will return to their regular work stations.

Fall B session final exams are scheduled for Monday and Tuesday (October 19-20), and Fall D session classes begin Monday. The college's Drop and Add period for D session concludes Tuesday. Faculty have been asked to extend deadlines and due dates for coursework and exams affected by the closure, and to remain flexible as campus operations ramp back up.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Libraries Reopen Monday After Hurricane Closures
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Three branches of the Santa Rosa County Library System will resume service Monday, October 19, following temporary closures caused by a recent hurricane. The Jay, Pace, and Gulf Breeze libraries will reopen during their regularly scheduled hours, while the Library Administration office will also resume operations. The reopened locations will offer…
item.content:encoded:
Three branches of the Santa Rosa County Library System will resume service Monday, October 19, following temporary closures caused by a recent hurricane. The Jay, Pace, and Gulf Breeze libraries will reopen during their regularly scheduled hours, while the Library Administration office will also resume operations.

The reopened locations will offer additional computer access to help residents navigate hurricane recovery—allowing community members to research assistance programs, complete online forms, and access critical information during the rebuilding effort.

Two other facilities remain closed. The Navarre Library continues experiencing storm-related power problems, while the Milton Library's previously planned October 19 reopening—originally scheduled after renovations—has been postponed to Monday, October 26 due to hurricane-related delays. The Family History & Research Center will remain closed until further notice as the county assesses conditions across the system.

Santa Rosa County Communications said staff will announce additional reopening dates as facilities are restored. Residents can call (850) 981-7323 or visit www.santarosa.fl.gov/libraries for updates.

The all-clear comes after water quality samples met safety requirements, allowing residents to use tap water normally again without boiling it…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County officials have rescinded the boil water notice for the Town of Jay as of Friday afternoon, following completion of bacteriological testing that confirmed the water supply is safe to drink.

The all-clear comes after water quality samples met safety requirements, allowing residents to use tap water normally again without boiling it first.

Meanwhile, boil water notices remain in effect for all customers of Bagdad Garcon Point Water. Residents in affected areas should continue to boil water before drinking or using it for cooking until they receive notice that their local system has been cleared.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott visits Cyprus to discuss Mediterranean security, energy ties
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott traveled to Cyprus today as part of a diplomatic visit focused on strengthening U.S. interests in the Mediterranean region. Scott, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and sits on the Foreign Relations Committee, met with U.S. Ambassador John Breslow and Cypriot Energy, Commerce, and Industry…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott traveled to Cyprus today as part of a diplomatic visit focused on strengthening U.S. interests in the Mediterranean region. Scott, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and sits on the Foreign Relations Committee, met with U.S. Ambassador John Breslow and Cypriot Energy, Commerce, and Industry Minister Michael Damianos to discuss expanding energy infrastructure between Europe and the Middle East.

During the visit, Scott toured the United Nations Buffer Zone that divides the island, reaffirming U.S. support for Cypriot sovereignty and calling out Turkish military occupation that has persisted since 1974. "A strong, reunified Cyprus makes it easier to do business in the region and counters the aggression we've seen from thugs like Putin and Erdogan," Scott said in a statement, noting that Turkey remains the principal obstacle to resolving the island's division.

Scott emphasized the strategic importance of a stable Mediterranean as the U.S. energy industry expands its presence in the region and energy flows between the Middle East and Europe increase. He called on Cyprus and other regional allies to strengthen their defenses to reduce reliance on U.S. military involvement overseas.

Pensacola residents should prepare for traffic delays and a significant police presence as the Pensacola Police Department holds an honor procession for Detective Angela Nieto, who was killed in a motorcycle crash.

The procession will move Nieto's body from the medical examiner's office to a funeral home. The police department is remembering one of their own with the ceremony, which is expected to draw a large law enforcement presence to the area.

Drivers in Escambia County should anticipate delays during the procession and plan alternate routes if possible. The Pensacola Police Department has not yet released specific timing or route details for the honor procession.

item.content:encoded: Fairhope Police Department officers have determined that a bomb threat reported in the area was actually a swatting call, according to WKRG-TV 5. The confirmation came after officers investigated the initial report and ruled out any credible threat.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott Calls for Spending Cuts, Debt Action in Latest 'Rescuing America' Push
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott released a video today calling on Congress to cut spending and tackle the nation's $40 trillion debt, arguing that both Democrats and Republicans share responsibility for fiscal irresponsibility. In the video, part of his "Rescuing America" project, Scott criticized what he called wasteful earmarks and said the federal…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott released a video today calling on Congress to cut spending and tackle the nation's $40 trillion debt, arguing that both Democrats and Republicans share responsibility for fiscal irresponsibility.

In the video, part of his "Rescuing America" project, Scott criticized what he called wasteful earmarks and said the federal government has become "completely unaccountable to taxpayers." He linked government spending to inflation and rising costs for housing, healthcare, and groceries, saying the national debt is "the leading reason why everything costs you so much more."

Scott's "Rescuing America" initiative centers on three stated goals: balancing the federal budget, cutting government regulations, and creating private-sector jobs. The senator has previously released videos on healthcare reform and homeownership as part of the broader campaign.

item.title: UWF Police Chief Among 19 Florida Criminal Justice Leaders Graduating Executive Seminar
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Chief Roman Jackson of the University of West Florida Police Department is among 19 criminal justice leaders from across Florida who have completed an intensive three-week executive training program designed to prepare them for top leadership roles. The graduates finished the Chief Executive Seminar, Class 59, run by the Florida Criminal Justice…
item.content:encoded:
Chief Roman Jackson of the University of West Florida Police Department is among 19 criminal justice leaders from across Florida who have completed an intensive three-week executive training program designed to prepare them for top leadership roles.

The graduates finished the Chief Executive Seminar, Class 59, run by the Florida Criminal Justice Executive Institute, which operates within the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. The program, established by the Florida Legislature in 1990, brings together criminal justice executives for coursework covering emerging challenges including future trends, social media management, stress management, succession planning, and trust-based leadership.

The seminar participants represent 17 agencies statewide. Beyond UWF, the class included leaders from the Broward Sheriff's Office, Florida Highway Patrol, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Polk County Sheriff's Office, and departments of corrections and juvenile justice, among others. The institute is affiliated with the State University System and offers multi-disciplinary education aimed at strengthening Florida's criminal justice leadership pipeline.

item.title: George Stone Technical College launches endowed scholarship in Stone family name
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: George Stone Technical College and Escambia County Public Schools will hold a ceremony today to formally announce the George G. and Pattie O. Stone Endowed Scholarship Fund, a permanent endowment established through an anonymous donation to support students at the technical college. The fund honors the Stone family's historical contributions to…
item.content:encoded:
George Stone Technical College and Escambia County Public Schools will hold a ceremony today to formally announce the George G. and Pattie O. Stone Endowed Scholarship Fund, a permanent endowment established through an anonymous donation to support students at the technical college.

The fund honors the Stone family's historical contributions to career and technical education in Northwest Florida. According to a press release from the school district, the ceremony—themed "A Legacy of Opportunity"—will include members of the Stone family, students, faculty, staff, district leadership, and other invited guests. The event will recognize the institution's history while highlighting what organizers say will be a transformational investment for future generations of George Stone Technical College students.

"This event is an opportunity to celebrate where George Stone Technical College came from while also looking toward its future," said Stephen Brooks, principal of the college. "The Stone name has represented opportunity in this community for generations. This endowment will ensure that legacy continues by helping future students pursue the education and training that can transform their lives."

George Stone Technical College, which traces its roots to vocational and technical education initiatives launched more than 50 years ago, currently prepares students for careers in high-demand fields and supports workforce development across Northwest Florida.

The facility provides access to a range of services aimed at helping affected residents rebuild. Visitors can seek help securing…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola opened the Bayview Multi-Agency Resource Center (MARC) on Thursday at 2000 E. Lloyd Street, offering residents a centralized hub for storm recovery assistance following recent hurricane impacts.

The facility provides access to a range of services aimed at helping affected residents rebuild. Visitors can seek help securing food, water, and housing, as well as broader recovery services and resources. According to a city announcement, the center is specifically designed to serve hurricane-impacted individuals seeking information and direct assistance.

The opening of the MARC represents the city's effort to consolidate recovery support in one location rather than directing residents to multiple agencies. Residents in need of storm-related help are encouraged to visit the center at 2000 E. Lloyd Street.

item.title: Santa Rosa County opens free vegetative debris drop-off sites
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is opening two temporary, free drop-off locations for residents to dispose of vegetative debris from Hurricane Isaias, offering an alternative to the county's ongoing curbside collection service. The sites are located at Lenny James Tolbert Memorial Park (Holley Ball Park) in Navarre at 3124 Bob Tolbert Road, and Santa Rosa…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is opening two temporary, free drop-off locations for residents to dispose of vegetative debris from Hurricane Isaias, offering an alternative to the county's ongoing curbside collection service.

The sites are located at Lenny James Tolbert Memorial Park (Holley Ball Park) in Navarre at 3124 Bob Tolbert Road, and Santa Rosa Soccer Park in Pace at 3360 Joppa Drive. Both operate from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., seven days a week, until further notice. The service is available at no cost to Santa Rosa County residents with valid ID or proof of residency.

The drop-off sites accept only vegetative storm debris, including tree limbs, branches, leaves, and yard waste. Residents cannot dispose of household garbage, construction debris, appliances, or commercial waste at these locations. Material in plastic bags will not be accepted; only paper bags are permitted. This option supplements the county's curbside debris pickup, which began Wednesday, October 14, along publicly owned roads.
